threads.body:
[Style] Match the ordering used in the 1.4 module (`library(...)` first).

```suggestion
  library("org.apache.hbase:hbase-client:1.0.0")

  implementation(project(":instrumentation:hbase:hbase-client-common-1.0:javaagent"))
```

Nothing from `ExperimentalInstrumentationModule` is overridden here — `isHelperClass` / `injectedClassNames` moved onto `InstrumentationModule` in #19142. Drop it (and the now-unused import), like the 2.0 module.

```suggestion
public class HbaseInstrumentationModule extends InstrumentationModule {
```

[General] `RpcCall10Advice` and `RpcCallLaterAdvice` have identical bodies apart from the argument indices. Extract the shared logic into an `AdviceScope` helper with `start()` / `end()` so each advice is a thin delegation — that also keeps the inlined bytecode small.

Did you consider hooking `AbstractRpcClient.callBlockingMethod` instead? Its signature is identical across 1.0.0–1.3.x (`md, pcrc, param, returnType, ticket, addr`), so one advice would cover the whole range and it would mirror how the 1.4 module hooks `callMethod`. If the reason is that it wraps exceptions in `ServiceException`, a short comment would help.

[General] Positional argument matchers are hard to follow — document the target signature.

```suggestion
    // 1.0.x: call(pcrc, md, param, cells, returnType, ticket, addr, rpcTimeout, priority)
    transformer.applyAdviceToMethod(
```

Worth noting here too why only the unshaded `MethodDescriptor` is matched (`hbase-shaded-client` starts at 1.1.0).

```suggestion
    // 1.1.0+: call(pcrc, md, param, returnType, ticket, addr[, callStats])
    transformer.applyAdviceToMethod(
```

This is an exact copy of the 1.4 class. Now that `hbase-client-common-1.0` compiles against 1.0.0 and both modules use the unshaded `ClientProtos`, it could move into the common module (2.0 keeps its shaded copy). Same applies to `HbaseSingletons.methodDescriptorName`.
[Testing] A short comment on why 1.0–1.3 surface a plain `IOException` here (the timeout is wrapped by `IPCUtil.wrapException`) would help.
[Testing] Can you add a comment on why 1.0–1.3 produce 3 scan traces where 1.4 produces 1? Also worth confirming the count is deterministic, otherwise this assertion could be flaky.

[General] This file is byte-identical to `hbase-client-1.4/.../v1_4/RetryingCallableInstrumentation.java` — the package declaration is literally the only differing line. Since this PR is already consolidating shared code into `hbase-client-common-1.0` (`HbaseBatchMetadata`, the new `HbaseClientUtil`), this one should move there too: it only depends on `HbaseClientState` and hbase-client 1.0 API, both available in the common module.

`TypeInstrumentation` classes living in a `*-common-*` javaagent module is an established pattern here (`netty-common-4.0`, `tomcat-common-7.0`, `servlet-common`, `jetty-common-8.0`), so both `HbaseInstrumentationModule`s can just instantiate the shared class. `hbase-client-2.0`'s `RegionServerCallableInstrumentation` has the same advice with only a different type matcher, so it could fold in as well if the matcher is made a constructor arg.

Anchoring here since the file itself isn't in the diff: `docs/supported-libraries.md` still lists HBase Client as `2.0 - 2.4.x`. Now that this PR covers `[1.0,1.4)`, that row should say `1.0 - 2.4.x` so the docs match what the agent actually instruments.
